title: Burst Fidelity Fallback Credit Framework
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
This playbook describes the "Burst Fidelity Fallback Credit Framework" — a pricing & packaging mechanism that issues short-duration microcredits when production inference requests fall back to lower-fidelity variants (quantized models, smaller variants, or degraded runtime paths) or when customers consume temporarily provisioned burst capacity (preemptible or on-demand warm pools). The goal is to: reduce customer surprise, preserve predictable unit economics, and provide a clear commercial mapping for degraded fidelity or burst usage.

Audience and goals
- Audience: Product managers, pricing, billing engineers, platform SRE, and sales/account teams.
- Business goals: minimize churn caused by unexpected quality changes, offer transparent cost signals for fidelity changes, and protect Redwood margins for burst/low-fidelity execution.
- Operational goals: telemetry alignment, automated credit issuance with audit trails, and simple migration path for existing customers.

When this applies
1) Fidelity fallback events: automatic or forced fallback from a primary variant to a lower-fidelity variant (examples: FP16 -> 4-bit quantized; base model variant -> distilled variant) triggered by the Fidelity Orchestrator due to capacity, latency, or policy.
2) Burst capacity usage: short-lived use of preemptible/warm capacity beyond committed reserved capacity.
3) Customer-requested emergency downgrade: explicit downgrade requested by a customer for cost/latency reasons.

Principles
- Transparency: customers see an immediate, itemized credit note in their Console activity stream and billing preview.
- Predictability: credits are expressed as small, discrete units (microcredits) that map to token-equivalents.
- Conservatism: credits compensate for visible fidelity degradation or burst economic delta, not for normal model variance.
- Auditor-friendly: every issued credit must include a traceable reason, timestamp, request-id(s), and the responsible service (fidelity-orchestrator/billing-core).

Key definitions
- Microcredit (MC): the atomic unit applied to invoice adjustments. 1 MC = 0.0001 credit-unit (internal accounting). MCs map to token-equivalents on the invoice UI.
- Fidelity downgrade event: a single inference request or a batch where the returned variant has measurable lower expected quality (by the fidelity classifier).
- Burst interval: contiguous time window where a tenant consumes > 120% of committed capacity and uses preemptible or warm pools to satisfy requests.

Rules and mapping (summary table)
| Trigger | Measured delta | Credit rule | Max per-request cap | Notes |
|--------|----------------|-------------|---------------------|-------|
| Automatic fidelity fallback (single request) | latency within SLO, quality delta >= 8% QA score | 5 MCs per 1k tokens affected | 200 MCs | Applies only when fallback is initiated by fidelity-orchestrator and tagged in telemetry |
| Sustained fidelity fallback (>=1m continuous for device pool) | observed QA delta >= 5% averaged | 200 MCs per minute per tenant | 5,000 MCs/day | Auto-credits emitted hourly; requires review if > threshold |
| Burst capacity usage (short burst <= 15m) | cost delta due to preemptible/warm pool vs reserved | 10 MCs per 1k tokens processed on burst-capacity | 1,000 MCs per burst | Burst must be signaled by capacity-manager with a burst-tag |
| Customer-requested downgrade | explicit customer API flag | prorated credits: 50% of automatic fallback credit | 500 MCs/day | Only when customer has requested and acknowledged potential quality change |

Eligibility and exclusions
- Eligible: paid tenants with active billing relationship (non-trial) and customers on hosted or dedicated plans.
- Excluded: test tenants, free-tier trials, synthetic or internal traffic (traffic marked by internal test-tag).
- Exempted: fallbacks caused by explicit model pinning mismatch (customer misconfiguration) — these are not auto-credited and are routed to Customer Success triage.

Telemetry and signals required (implementation checklist)
1) fidelity-orchestrator must emit event: fidelity.fallback {tenant_id, request_id, original_variant, fallback_variant, qa_delta, affected_tokens, trace_id, timestamp}
2) capacity-manager must emit event: capacity.burst {tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, pool_type, estimated_cost_delta, trace_id}
3) billing-core must subscribe to the above events and produce credit.emit events with audit metadata.
4) Console must display "Credit transactions" with filter by reason and include links to the specific request traces.

Billing and UI mapping
- Credits are applied to the monthly invoice as line-item adjustments with a code: BF-FB-<rule-id>.
- Console preview: when a credit is detected within the current billing cycle, customers see an estimated credit and the reason (e.g., "Auto-credit: fidelity fallback — quantized variant.").
- Notifications: email or webhook can be configured (default: email for enterprise accounts).

Sample credit emission flow (sequence)
1) fidelity-orchestrator detects fallback for request R and emits fidelity.fallback event.
2) billing-core receives event, validates tenant eligibility and computes MCs per rule table.
3) billing-core emits credit.emit event and stores credit record (credit_id, tenant_id, amount_mc, reason, associated_traces).
4) Console ingests credit records and surfaces in Billing -> Adjustments.
5) If credits > 5,000 MC/day for tenant, alert on PagerDuty to finance/ps-reviews for manual review.

API/CLI example (internal billing-core call)
Request JSON example (billing-core incoming webhook):
{
  "event_type": "fidelity.fallback",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_45b2",
  "request_id": "req_9a3f",
  "original_variant": "redwood-1.0-base",
  "fallback_variant": "redwood-1.0-quant4",
  "qa_delta": 9.2,
  "affected_tokens": 420,
  "timestamp": "2029-06-21T15:22:10Z"
}

Billing-core credit emit example (internal audit record):
{
  "credit_id": "C-20290621-7f9",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_45b2",
  "mc_amount": 210,
  "reason": "fidelity_fallback_auto",
  "associated_requests": ["req_9a3f"],
  "emitted_at": "2029-06-21T15:22:11Z"
}

Configuration examples (storefront mapping YAML)
storefront_credit_rules:
  fidelity_fallback:
    per_1k_tokens: 5
    min_mc: 5
    max_per_request: 200
  burst_capacity:
    per_1k_tokens: 10
    burst_window_seconds: 900
    max_per_burst: 1000

Acceptance criteria and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (pilot, 4 weeks): enable auto-credits for 10 low-risk tenants (opt-in via enterprise console). Verify telemetry completeness and credit accuracy within ±10%.
- Phase 1 (controlled ramp, 8 weeks): expand to 200 tenants and enable credit visibility in Console. Integrate accounting reconciliations with finance ledger.
- Phase 2 (general availability): enable for all eligible paid tenants. Expose opt-out for customers who prefer no auto-credits (sales/legal sign-off required).

KPIs and guardrails
- Credit accuracy: >= 95% match between computed credits and manual audit sample.
- Cost exposure: daily credits issued should not exceed 0.5% of monthly MRR in GA. Finance alert if approaching 0.3% of monthly MRR in a single week.
- Telemetry completeness: fidelity.fallback events must be present for >= 99% of identified fallback requests.

Operational runbooks (quick play)
- If credits spike for a tenant: check fidelity.orchestrator logs, confirm fallback reason, validate whether an incident or rolling deploy triggered increases. If customer impact, notify CS and apply manual remediation credits if appropriate.
- If billing-core fails to emit credit events: route to oncall-sre and escalate to billing-engineering. Backfill window: allowed up to 72 hours, beyond that requires finance approval.

Owner and governance
- Product owner: Maya Chen (product).
- Implementing teams: billing-engineering (owner), fidelity-orchestrator (owner), capacity-manager (owner), console (owner).
- Finance steward: Aaron Lee (finance).
- Legal reviewer: Priya Nair (go-to-market counsel).

Open questions and future work
- Should credits be convertible to usage-bonuses for committed customers (trade credits for extra reserved capacity)? (Finance + Sales decision)
- Granular per-route fidelity credits vs. per-tenant credits: tradeoff between bookkeeping complexity and customer clarity.
- Explore machine-learning classifier to predict and pre-issue credits for probable fallbacks during deploy windows.

References and related artifacts
- Implementation spec: /product-docs/design-specs/quantization-cache-fidelity-coordination-spec-2026-11-15 (implementation notes).
- Billing integration: /product-docs/design-specs/consumption-telemetry-provenance-and-crediting-spec-2029-12-05.
- Pilot tenants and opt-in list: internal doc (finance ledger ID: FL-2029-BF-01).

Appendix: sample scenarios
- Scenario A (single-request fallback): customer A sends a 2k token request. Fidelity orchestrator falls back due to node eviction; qa_delta = 10%. Credit issued = 2k/1k * 5 MC = 10 MCs. Customer sees line-item: "Auto-credit: fidelity fallback — quantized variant — 10 MC".
- Scenario B (short burst): tenant B uses warm pool for 12 minutes during traffic surge; processing 120k tokens. Credit issued = 120 * 10 MC = 1200 MCs; capped at per-burst max 1000 MC so 1000 MCs applied.
